newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan letter bomb sent to popular TV news woman.
newsitem.headline: Japan letter bomb sent to popular TV news woman.

text.p: A letter bomb addressed to a popular female newscaster exploded at her Tokyo television station's headquarters on Wednesday, injuring one person.
A spokesman for Nippon Television Network Corp said the letter was addressed to Yumi Ida, 39, a highly rated late evening news anchor.
The bomb was in an envelope containing what appeared to be a videotape.
The spokesman said the blast left Masamichi Maeda, 52, manager of the station's department of services to viewers, with wounds to his head and a thumb.
There were no claims of responsibility for the attack.
Nippon Television is affiliated with Japan's biggest newspaper, the Yomiuri Shimbun.
In December 1994, a parcel bomb addressed to a popular young actress exploded at the same television station, injuring two people.
